newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet day slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet day slightly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished lower after a very quiet session.
Tame U.S. January consumer price data and the death of China's 92-year-old leader had no lasting effect in U.S. fixed income markets.

"A lot of the guys I'm talking to have no idea and no desire to trade this market," one Eurodollar futures trader said. "It's always the quietest before the storm and I'm hoping that's where we are, but it is just dead down here right now," he added.
Traders said March T-bond trade was equally quiet.

"We really didn't see much today," said Mike Boss, a vice president with Dean Witter Reynolds. "Profit-taking and fund selling (in the cash market) put weight on the market and we were never able to recover," he said.
But overall, Boss said the market was still in an uptrend. He pegged support at 113-8/32 and resistance at 115-16/32.

Early in the session, January CPI was released and many traders took it to paint a subdued inflation picture. But strength from the report was very short-lived. Jan CPI rose 0.1 percent overall and 0.1 percent excluding volatile food and energy sectors.
Wall Street had forecast Jan CPI up 0.3 percent overall and up 0.2 percent ex-food and energy. In the previous report, overall CPI rose 0.3 percent and the core rate gained a revised 0.2 percent.
In the short end, floor traders lamented light volume and tight ranges.
"There were no good flows in here," one IMM trader remarked. "It was very quiet -- especially for a CPI day."
He said one Wall Street firm sold 4,000 June Eurodollar contracts to add to their Tuesday sales. Another Euro broker cited June/June spread activity.
He noted several Wall Street firms who were sellers of 1,000 each September contracts.
"Dealers were sellers of Sep and a lot of those same people were also big buyers in the June/June spread from anything from 500 to 1000 contracts," he said.
Debt futures paid no attention to a 2.0-percent drop in U.S. January real earnings.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were down 7/32 to 113-20/32, 10-year notes were off 5/32 to 110-2/32, March T-bills were flat at 95.03, June Euros were steady at 94.41 and September was down one bp at 94.29.
